mainTopic: Forced sales: the limits on רב הונא's rule, the final הלכה, forced קידושין, and the story of טאבי and פאפי
overview: This amud continues the discussion of רב הונא's rule that a sale made under pressure (תליוהו וזבין) still counts. The גמרא first adds three limits, one after another: the sale might fail if one specific field was named, the money was not counted, and the seller had no way out. Then it rules that the sale is valid in every case, even for a specific field. Its proof is אמימר's ruling that forced קידושין take effect, since a woman is like 'this field.' מר בר רב אשי disagrees. He says the רבנן cancel forced קידושין as a penalty, so the proof does not work. When רבינא asks how this works with ביאה, רב אשי answers that the רבנן treat it as בעילת זנות. Next comes the story of טאבי, who hung up פאפי until he sold, while רבה בר בר חנה signed both פאפי's מודעא and the bill of sale. רב הונא approves of both signatures, and the גמרא explains that without the מודעא the bill of sale would have been valid. Finally the גמרא begins to ask, from רב נחמן's ruling about witnesses who call their document an אמנה, how a witness can undo a document he signed. That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The rule may cover only an unspecified field
steps.stepSummary: The forced-sale rule is limited to where the seller was forced to sell 'a field' in general, not 'this field.'
steps.simpleTranslation: [We only said the forced sale is valid] when he was forced to sell 'a field' in general. But if he was forced to sell 'this field,' the sale is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts a first limit on רב הונא's rule that a forced sale is valid. The rule may apply only when the seller was told to sell 'a field' and could pick which one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seller could choose which field to sell, part of the decision was still his own, so we say he really agreed to the sale. If the person pressuring him named one specific field, the seller chose nothing, so the sale does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: An unspecified field, where the seller picks which one
'This field': one specific field named by the person forcing the sale
'They hung him and he sold': a sale made under heavy pressure

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final הלכה. It is the first of three limits, and in step 4 the גמרא rejects all of them.

phrases.english: [only] in a case of 'a field' unspecified,
but in a case of 'this field' – no.

steps.triggerLanguage: בשדה סתם, אבל בשדה זו לא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב הונא's forced-sale rule from the earlier text
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A forced sale is valid only when the field was unspecified. If one specific field was named, the sale is invalid.

steps.title: Even 'this field' is valid if the seller counted the money
steps.stepSummary: A second limit: the sale of a specific field is invalid only if the seller did not count the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even with 'this field,' we only said the sale is invalid when he did not count the money. But if he counted the money, it is not invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the first limit. A forced sale of one specific field is invalid only if the seller did not count the money he was paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting the money carefully shows that the seller cared about the payment and accepted the deal. So even when the field was named for him, counting the money makes the sale valid.

keyTerms.meaning: He counted the coins
'We did not say': a formula that limits an earlier statement

phrases.english: And even in 'this field,' we only said [the sale is invalid]
where he did not count the money,
but if he counted the money – no [it is not invalid].

steps.triggerLanguage: ובשדה זו נמי לא אמרן אלא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the 'this field' exception from step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the seller counted the money, the sale of a specific field is valid.

steps.title: Only invalid if the seller had no way to escape
steps.stepSummary: A third limit: the sale is invalid only if the seller could not have avoided the pressure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we only said the sale is invalid when he had no way to slip out of it. But if he had a way to slip out, it is not invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more limit. The sale is invalid only if the seller truly had no way to get out of the pressure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seller could have escaped and chose not to, his staying in the deal shows he went along with it. So the sale stands.

keyTerms.meaning: To slip away, to escape or avoid something

steps.whatToRemember: There are three limits, each one narrower than the last. Before the final ruling, the sale fails only when all three are true: one specific field was named, the seller did not count the money, and he had no way to escape. In step 4 the גמרא rules the sale valid even then.

phrases.english: And we only said [the sale is invalid]
where he had no way to slip out,
but if he had a way to slip out – no.

steps.triggerLanguage: ולא אמרן אלא דלא הוה לאישתמוטי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the invalid case even further
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the seller could have avoided the pressure, the sale is valid.

steps.title: The final ruling: the sale is valid in every case
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that a forced sale is valid in all the cases above, even for 'this field.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה in all these cases is that his sale is a valid sale, even with 'this field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final הלכה. A forced sale counts in every case discussed, including when one specific field was named.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets aside the limits from steps 1–3. Even the strongest case, a named field with no money counted and no way out, is still a valid sale.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is
His sale is a valid sale
In all of them

steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: a sale under pressure is valid, even for a specific field.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for sales made under pressure.

phrases.english: And the הלכה in all of them
is that his sale is a valid sale,
and even in 'this field'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets aside the three limits and rules the sale valid in every case
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A forced sale is valid in every case, even for a specific named field.

steps.title: Proof from forced קידושין
steps.stepSummary: A woman is like 'this field,' and אמימר rules that קידושין done under pressure are valid, so a forced sale of a specific field is valid too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because a woman is like 'this field,' and אמימר said: if they hung her and he betrothed her, his קידושין are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the final ruling from אמימר's ruling about קידושין done under pressure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In קידושין the woman has no choice about who the man is. The man is fixed, just like a field that was named. Since אמימר rules that forced קידושין still take effect, a forced sale of one named field must also take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Is like, is comparable to
They hung her (put heavy pressure on her) and he betrothed her
His betrothal is a valid betrothal
אמימר, an אמורא whose ruling is quoted as the proof

phrases.english: for a woman is like 'this field,'
and אמימר said:
If they hung her and he betrothed her,
phrases.notes: 'Hung' here means she was put under heavy pressure until she agreed.

phrases.english: his betrothal is a valid betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the final ruling of step 4
steps.raayaObject: That a forced sale of a specific field is valid
steps.raayaSupportSource: אמימר's ruling that קידושין done under pressure are valid, since a woman is like 'this field'

steps.title: In a woman's case the קידושין are cancelled anyway
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי says forced קידושין are certainly not valid, because the רבנן cancelled them. So the proof from אמימר falls away.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: With a woman, the קידושין are certainly not valid. He acted improperly, so the רבנן acted improperly with him and took his קידושין away from him.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי pushes back on the proof from step 5. He says that when a woman is forced into קידושין, the קידושין do not stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said a woman is like 'this field', so if forced קידושין work, a forced sale of a specific field works too. מר בר רב אשי breaks the proof. With a woman, the רבנן step in and cancel the קידושין as a penalty, so nothing can be learned from her about forced sales.

keyTerms.meaning: Improperly, not the right way
The רבנן cancelled (literally, uprooted) it
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

steps.confusionAlert: מר בר רב אשי does not say forced קידושין fail on their own terms. He says the רבנן actively cancelled them as a penalty for how the man behaved.

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
With a woman, the betrothal is certainly not valid;
phrases.notes: He means a woman who was forced to accept the קידושין, the case from step 5.

phrases.english: he acted improperly,
therefore they acted improperly with him –
and the Sages cancelled his betrothal from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: בְּאִשָּׁה וַדַּאי קִדּוּשִׁין לָא הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from forced קידושין brought in step 5
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between a forced woman and a forced sale of 'this field'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: With a woman, the רבנן cancel the קידושין as a penalty, so her case teaches nothing about forced sales

steps.title: How can the רבנן cancel קידושין done through ביאה?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks: cancelling makes sense if he used money, but what can be said if he used ביאה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: This works if he betrothed her with money. But if he betrothed her through ביאה, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the idea that the רבנן can cancel any forced קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With money, the רבנן can take the money away from the man, and then the קידושין fall apart. With ביאה there is no money to take away, so it is not clear how the רבנן could cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out fine (for one case)
Money
Marital relations, one of the ways to make קידושין

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
This works where he betrothed with money,
if he betrothed through intercourse, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח דְּקַדֵּישׁ בְּכַסְפָּא, קַדֵּישׁ בְּבִיאָה מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the mechanism of cancellation proposed in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רבנן can cancel any forced קידושין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cancelling works through taking away the money, but with ביאה there is no money to take away

steps.title: The רבנן treated the ביאה as בעילת זנות
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the רבנן declared his ביאה to be בעילת זנות, which makes no קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The רבנן made his ביאה into בעילת זנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן do not need money to take away. They declare the act itself to be בעילת זנות instead of a ביאה of קידושין, so it never creates קידושין. This covers every way of making קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: They made it into, they deemed it
Relations with no marriage bond, which make no קידושין

steps.whatToRemember: According to מר בר רב אשי and רב אשי, forced קידושין are cancelled by the רבנן. With money they take away the money. With ביאה they treat it as בעילת זנות.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The Sages deemed his intercourse licentious intercourse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שַׁוְּיוּהּ רַבָּנַן לִבְעִילָתוֹ בְּעִילַת זְנוּת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different way the רבנן can cancel the קידושין
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cancelling works only by taking away the money, so ביאה cannot be cancelled
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן can declare the ביאה to be בעילת זנות, so it makes no קידושין

steps.title: The story of טאבי and פאפי
steps.stepSummary: טאבי hung פאפי up until he sold his field. רבה בר בר חנה signed both on פאפי's מודעא and on the bill of sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: טאבי hung פאפי on a כינרא, and פאפי sold. רבה בר בר חנה signed on the מודעא and on the bill of sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about a forced sale. It is setting up רב הונא's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before selling, פאפי made a מודעא, a statement that he was selling only because he was forced. רבה בר בר חנה then signed both that statement and the bill of sale. These two papers seem to say opposite things, and this sets up the question that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Hung (someone) up
A statement made beforehand to witnesses, saying 'I am being forced to sell'
Bill of sale
He sold

phrases.english: Tavi hung Pafi on a kinara, and he sold.
phrases.notes: The כינרא is something פאפי was hung on. The point is that he was under heavy pressure until he agreed to sell his field.

phrases.aramaic: חֲתַם רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אַמּוֹדָעָא, וְאַאַשְׁקָלְתָּא.
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana signed on the declaration, and on the bill of sale.
phrases.notes: The declaration (מודעא) says the sale is forced and shouldn't count; the bill of sale says it does. He signed both.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case about a forced sale
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out the case: a sale made under pressure, with both a מודעא and a bill of sale signed by the same witness

steps.title: רב הונא praises both signatures
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says that whoever signed the מודעא did well, and whoever signed the bill of sale did well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Whoever signed on the מודעא signed well, and whoever signed on the bill of sale signed well.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives his view of what רבה בר בר חנה did and approves of both signatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying both signatures were proper is surprising, because the two papers seem to contradict each other. This statement is what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: He signed well, he did the right thing by signing

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
whoever signed on the declaration – signed well,
and whoever signed on the bill of sale – signed well.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מַאן דְּחָתֵים אַמּוֹדָעָא שַׁפִּיר חָתֵים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the case told in step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both the signature on the מודעא and the signature on the bill of sale were proper

steps.title: Both papers cannot be right
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the מודעא counts, the bill of sale does not, and if the bill of sale counts, the מודעא does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it: if the מודעא counts, there is no bill of sale. If the bill of sale counts, there is no מודעא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא for approving two papers that cancel each other out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מודעא cancels the sale, and a bill of sale makes it stand. Only one of them can have an effect, so it seems one of the signatures must have been wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it (a two-sided challenge)

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it?
If there is a declaration – no bill of sale,
and if a bill of sale – no declaration!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה נַפְשָׁךְ? אִי מוֹדָעָא לָא אַשְׁקָלְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's statement in step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's approval of both signatures
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two papers contradict each other, so both signatures cannot be proper

steps.title: What רב הונא really meant
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא meant that if there had been no מודעא, signing the bill of sale would be proper.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: If not for the מודעא, whoever signed on the bill of sale signed well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב הונא's words so that they no longer contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the מודעא wins and cancels the sale. Still, the bill of sale was not a wrong thing to sign. Without the מודעא, a sale made under pressure would be valid, so the bill of sale would be a proper paper.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means
If not for

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
if not for the declaration,
whoever signed on the bill of sale – signed well.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא said both papers have an effect at the same time
steps.terutzMaskana: The מודעא cancels the sale. Without it, the bill of sale would have been valid, so signing it was proper

steps.title: רב הונא follows his own view: a forced sale is valid
steps.stepSummary: This fits רב הונא's ruling elsewhere that if someone was hung up and sold, the sale is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא follows his own reasoning, as רב הונא said: If they hung him up and he sold, his sale is a sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the answer in step 12 matches another ruling of רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 assumed that without a מודעא, a forced sale would be valid. רב הונא says exactly this elsewhere: even a man hung up until he sells has made a real sale. So the explanation fits his known view.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning
His sale is a sale, the sale is valid

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא, a sale made under pressure is valid, even if the seller was hung up. Only a מודעא made beforehand can cancel it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This connects the story back to the main topic of the דף. It shows how strong the rule is that a forced sale is valid unless the seller made a מודעא.

phrases.english: Rav Huna follows his own reasoning –
as Rav Huna said:
If they hung him and he sold – his sale is a sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא לְטַעְמֵיהּ דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the explanation in step 12 with another ruling of רב הונא
steps.raayaObject: The assumption that, without a מודעא, the bill of sale would be valid
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא's ruling: תליוהו וזבין זביניה זביני

steps.title: Can a witness undo a document he himself signed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבה בר בר חנה's signature on the מודעא can really cancel the bill of sale he also signed. It begins quoting רב נחמן about witnesses who say their document was only an אמנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רב נחמן said: witnesses who said, 'Our statement was only a trust document'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging the idea that one witness can sign both the protest and the sale, letting the protest cancel the sale. It is setting up the challenge by starting to quote רב נחמן, and the end of his ruling comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר בר חנה signed the bill of sale, so he gave it his backing. If his מודעא cancels that sale, he is undoing his own signature. רב נחמן's case of witnesses who later say 'it was only an אמנה' is about exactly this kind of witness, and it will show they are not believed to undo their own document.

keyTerms.meaning: "Is that so?" An expression of surprise that opens a challenge
"But didn't he say..." introduces a source that seems to contradict
Witnesses who signed a document
A trust document: a loan document written ahead of time on trust, before any real loan was given

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן's sentence is not finished here. The words 'they are not believed' come in the next line, so do not try to find the ruling in this step.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
phrases.notes: The גמרא is surprised that רבה בר בר חנה's protest could cancel a sale he himself signed.

phrases.english: But didn't רב נחמן say:
Witnesses who said
"Our statement was only a trust document" –
phrases.notes: They mean the loan document they signed was written on trust, before any money was actually lent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After steps 12-13 explained רב הונא's ruling, the גמרא goes back to the story in step 9 and questions how רבה בר בר חנה's double signature could work.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption from steps 9-10 that רבה בר בר חנה's signature on the מודעא can cancel the bill of sale he also signed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A witness cannot undo a document he signed. רב נחמן's ruling about witnesses who later call their document an אמנה shows this, so how can רבה בר בר חנה's מודעא cancel his own signed sale?
